articles.title: Paleoantropologiczna sensacja. Odkryto kolejne kości denisowian

Wśród nich po raz pierwszy zidentyfikowano kość promieniową, jedną z dwóch długich kości przedramienia, należącą do przedstawiciela tej grupy. Znalezisko datowane na późny środkowy plejstocen, rzuca nowe światło na fizyczne cechy i zasięg geograficzny tej tajemniczej grupy homininów, której szczątki do tej pory były niezwykle rzadkie. Wyniki badań, opublikowane w prestiżowym czasopiśmie naukowym "Nature", stanowią ważny krok w kierunku poznania historii naszego gatunku i jego bliskich krewnych.

articles.title: Roame (YC S23) Is Hiring Viral Content Editor
articles.originalTitle: Roame (YC S23) Is Hiring Viral Content Editor
articles.excerpt:
About Roame

Roame is a flight and hotel search engine for points and miles.

Booking business or first class with points instead of cash saves travelers thousands of dollars on a single trip. The hard part is finding the seats. Award space is scattered across dozens of airline and hotel programs, it moves constantly, and the best deals get taken. Doing it by hand means hours across a dozen browser tabs, and often days.

Roame finds those deals in seconds. Members also book hotels through us and get our commission rebated back to them immediately. Roame was founded by Tim and Zi. Tim spent the previous decade covering consumer and travel companies on the hedge fund side. Zi ran data encryption systems at Airbnb.

We started Roame after losing dozens of hours hunting for first class award space to Asia across a dozen browser tabs. Award travel is a data problem. Humans shouldn't have to solve it by hand.

About the Role

We're hiring a Content Editor to build and run the machine that produces our video content — not just to edit clips.

The distinction matters. We're not looking for someone who takes a brief, opens Premiere, and disappears for two days. We're looking for someone who designs a repeatable template for a content format, figures out which parts of it a machine can produce (b-roll, motion graphics, screen recordings, captions, voice, variants, cutdowns) and which parts need a real human on camera or on mic, and then assembles those two halves into something that doesn't feel assembled.

If you've ever looked at your own editing workflow and thought "I'm doing this same 40 minutes of work every single time, I should systematize it" — this is that job.

One thing to be upfront about: we're in the business of extremely informative, time-sensitive content. A transfer bonus, a mistake fare, an award chart devaluation — these are worth a lot on day one and nothing by day four. Speed is everything. Good and out today beats perfect next week, every time. If what you want is a deeper artistic vision and the runway to chase it, this is not the right role and you'll be frustrated here.

Ideally, you also know how to grow an audience. We want someone with real instincts for what goes viral and how a channel compounds — not just clean edits, but follower growth, reach, and the kind of content that gets shared. We're starting this as a contract engagement, but the intent is that the right person grows into a full-time, key member of the team who owns Roame's audience end to end.

What You'll Own

Build the templates. Define repeatable formats for our recurring content: deal breakdowns, route explainers, product walkthroughs, founder/creator talking-head pieces, UGC-style ads. Each format gets a documented structure — hook patterns, pacing, caption style, motion system, asset library, project template — so episode #40 takes a fraction of the time episode #1 did.

Run the AI layer. Use generative tools for the tedious 70%: b-roll and stock replacement, generated visuals, voice cleanup and synthesis, auto-transcription and subtitling, silence removal, rough cuts from transcript, variant generation for ad testing. You should be opinionated about which tools are actually good and ruthless about which ones produce slop.

Stitch in the human parts. Coach and capture the human-recorded pieces — talking head, VO, screen recordings, phone footage — and blend them with generated material so the seams don't show. Knowing when not to use AI is as much of this job as knowing when to.

Shoot on location. We make destination content — hotels, lounges, cabins, cities. You may be asked to go on trips to shoot it, and to be on camera yourself. This isn't a behind-the-lens-only role: we're looking for someone comfortable being a personality in the content, not just the person cutting it. Travel and hotels are covered.

Produce the volume. Ship short-form for Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts, plus longer YouTube pieces and paid social creative. Multiple pieces a week, not a month.

Close the loop. Watch retention curves and ad performance, find where people drop, and feed that back into the templates. Hooks get iterated, not guessed at.

Keep the system usable by others. Document workflows, maintain the asset and preset library, and build things anyone on the team can pick up — so the machine doesn't stop when you're on vacation.

What We're Looking For

  - You're fast, and you ship. Same-day turnarounds are normal here. You know when a piece is good enough to go out and you don't sit on it.
  - You build systems, not just files. You think in templates, presets, naming conventions, and reusable components. You get visibly annoyed by repeated manual work.
  - Real editing chops. Premiere / Final Cut / DaVinci / CapCut — whatever you use, the output has to be sharp. Motion and animation ability (After Effects or equivalent) is a big plus.
  - Fluent with AI video tooling. Generative video and image, AI voice, transcript-based editing, auto-captioning, upscaling, cleanup. You've already built at least one workflow that chains several of these together.
  - Taste, specifically for short-form. You can watch a cut and say exactly where it loses people and why. You understand hooks, pacing, retention, and what makes something feel native to a feed vs. like an ad.
  - Real shooting sense. Framing, lighting, audio. You can travel light, set up a clean creator rig in a hotel room, and come home with usable footage without a crew.
  - A growth instinct. You understand what makes something spread, and you've got a point of view on how to take an account from where it is to where it should be. Bonus if you've done it before, for yourself or someone else.
  - Comfortable on camera. Or willing to get there fast.
  - Ownership. Small team, fast pace. You'll pick the format, make the call, ship it, and report on it — nobody is going to hand you a shot list.

Nice to Have

  - You already care about points, miles, or travel (or you're the kind of person who will go deep on it in week one)
  - Experience editing UGC and direct-response ad creative, not just brand pieces
  - Design system fluency — you can hold a consistent visual language across dozens of pieces
  - Light scripting or automation (batch processing, ffmpeg, API-driven pipelines, agent tooling)
  - You've grown an account of your own and know what actually moved it

How to Apply

  - Three pieces of work you're proud of. Links, not attachments.
  - One workflow teardown. Pick something you've made that mixed AI-generated and human-recorded material. Walk us through the template: what was generated, what was shot, what tools, how long it took, and how long it would take you on the tenth one.
  - A one-liner on why Roame.
